old_findings.note: In claimRedeem the loop's requires now print 'unknown request' / 'epoch not settled', the transfers are asset.transfer(..) with arguments, SafeERC20FailedOperation is 'revert with 0x5274afe7, _146'. Still: epochs[concat(mem[0])] keys (P4 25) and recipients split as 'Bytes(28, ..), Bytes(4, uint32(..))'.

regressions.decompiled:
_5 = mem[64]
...
while s < mem[128]:
    ...
return memory from mem[64] len _5 - mem[64] + 128 * stor4[_address].length + 64
regressions.source: returns the caller's withdrawal requests (struct array copied from storage to memory, then ABI-encoded)
regressions.issue: mem[128] = stor4[_address].length is no longer forwarded past the copy loop, whose writes all lie at or above mem[64] (at least 160), so the encode loop tests a memory word; and '_5 - mem[64]' (0) is left in the return length.
regressions.rule: A loop-carried mem[64] that starts at a known floor and only grows keeps that floor, so stores through it cannot reach lower constant addresses; and a variable holding mem[64] equals mem[64] until the next write to word 64 (fold the difference).

improvements: claimRedeem (unknown2370e069) 143 -> 89 lines: string reverts in the loop, named asset.transfer calls with arguments, custom error with its argument, the event data as values, direct return-data reverts, dead writes gone (P2 2 -> 0). unknownb26b9efc's Initializable slot prints as 0xf0c57e16...00 instead of a constant times 3600 (P1 2 -> 0). P6 12 -> 0.
notes: Reviewed function by function (247-line diff, 9 functions, 6 display-only). Calls, logs, requires and storage writes unchanged.
summary: One low regression (getUserWithdrawalRequests reads the array length back from memory and keeps an unfolded '_5 - mem[64]'); claimRedeem is much clearer and the P1/P2/P6 patterns are gone.
